BACnet Function Code and Service Choice Reference
=================================================

Scope
-----
This file contains standardized BACnet protocol operation identifiers:

1. BACnet APDU PDU Type
2. Confirmed Service Choice
3. Unconfirmed Service Choice
4. BACnet/IP BVLC Function
5. BACnet/IP BVLC Result Code
6. BACnet Network Layer Message Type
7. Reject Reason
8. Abort Reason
9. Error Class

The values marked RESERVED must not be interpreted as currently defined
standard operations.

================================================================
1. BACnet APDU PDU TYPE
================================================================

The APDU type is stored in the high nibble of the first APDU octet.

0x00 = Confirmed-Request-PDU
0x10 = Unconfirmed-Request-PDU
0x20 = SimpleACK-PDU
0x30 = ComplexACK-PDU
0x40 = SegmentACK-PDU
0x50 = Error-PDU
0x60 = Reject-PDU
0x70 = Abort-PDU

PDU type numeric value before shifting:

0 = Confirmed-Request-PDU
1 = Unconfirmed-Request-PDU
2 = SimpleACK-PDU
3 = ComplexACK-PDU
4 = SegmentACK-PDU
5 = Error-PDU
6 = Reject-PDU
7 = Abort-PDU

================================================================
2. BACnet CONFIRMED SERVICE CHOICE
================================================================

[SOURCE id=issue:1270:1270-summary:f10b3cba62a1 kind=issue issue=1270 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#1270.txt]
Issue: 1270
Summary: In v1.3.1, the report says a malformed UCOV/property-value payload can make bacapp_decode_application_data() accept an oversized extended application length without checking it against the remaining APDU bytes. That unchecked length is then propagated through bacapp_decode_data() into host_n_port_decode(), which trusts it, and bacnet_tag_number_decode() eventually performs an invalid read and crashes. The observed result was an AddressSanitizer SEGV; GDB showed apdu_len_max=12, tag_len=7, len_value_type=0xFF210121, and tag_data_type=34 (BACNET_APPLICATION_TAG_HOST_N_PORT).
Reproduce: 1) Use v1.3.1. 2) Decode a malformed UCOV/property-value payload whose extended application length exceeds the remaining APDU bytes; the reported bytes near the triggering boundary were: f5 22 ff ff 21 01 21 0e 2d ff 00 e6. 3) In the failing case, GDB showed apdu_len_max=12, tag_len=7, len_value_type=0xFF210121, and tag_data_type=34 (BACNET_APPLICATION_TAG_HOST_N_PORT). 4) Expected result: the oversized length is accepted by bacapp_decode_application_data(), passed via bacapp_decode_data() into host_n_port_decode(), and bacnet_tag_number_decode() hits an invalid read, with AddressSanitizer reporting SEGV on an unknown address 0x641f9505e92e (pc 0x641f93a5ffdd bp 0x7ffeab919b70 sp 0x7ffeab919b50 T0).
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-62973:cve-2026-62973-summa:7487fbadc732 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-62973.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-62973
Summary: In bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6, the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm is vulnerable while parsing ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK messages in bip_receive() -> npdu_handler() -> apdu_handler() -> My_Read_Property_Multiple_Ack_Handler() -> rpm_ack_decode_service_request(). A malicious BACnet/IP peer can answer a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request with a malformed but structurally valid ACK whose property-value [4] for start-time(142) contains a valid BACnetDateTime, then a semantically invalid application BOOLEAN, plus filler NULL tags. On failure, rpm_ack_decode_service_request() resets len to the full enclosed tag-4 payload length returned by bacnet_enclosed_data_length() instead of the remaining unconsumed length, advances apdu/apdu_len past the end of the global receive buffer Rx_Buf, and then calls bacnet_is_closing_tag_number() with the now-negative signed apdu_len, which is consumed as an unsigned size. The reproduced outcome is a global-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read on Rx_Buf; the source says the first invalid read is apdu[0] in bacnet_tag_number_decode(), and the verified impact is remote client-side denial of service.
Reproduce: 1) Use apps/readpropm from bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6 as the client. 2) Start the Python 3 UDP PoC bound to 127.0.0.1:47808. 3) Have readpropm send a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to that BACnet/IP peer. 4) When the PoC receives the request, copy request byte 8 as invoke_id and reply to the sender with a BVLC 0x81 0x0A frame whose NPDU/APDU prefix is 01 00 30 <invoke_id> 0E and whose body is a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK containing object-identifier device:123, list-of-results opening tag 1, propertyIdentifier start-time(142), and property-value
[/SOURCE]

<invoke_id> 0E and whose body is a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK containing object-identifier device:123, list-of-results opening tag 1, propertyIdentifier start-time(142), and property-value opening tag 4 with one valid BACnetDateTime (2024-01-01 weekday 1 and 00:00:00.00), then application BOOLEAN true, then NULL filler bytes chosen so the full frame length is MAX_BVLC_FRAME 1506, followed by closing tag 4 and closing tag 1. 5) Expected result: the reply reaches bip_receive() -> npdu_handler() -> apdu_handler() -> My_Read_Property_Multiple_Ack_Handler() -> rpm_ack_decode_service_request() and, per the source, triggers an ASan global-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read on Rx_Buf; the first invalid access is apdu[0] in bacnet_tag_number_decode(), causing client-side denial of service.
